rds.visuals-in-text overlaps dat.reading-graphs and dat.reading-tables. I linked dat.referring-to-visuals <- rds.visuals-in-text (soft). Recommend rds.visuals-in-text take dat.reading-graphs and dat.reading-tables as soft prerequisites and not depend on any DAT writing topic, to avoid cycles.

res.results, res.quantitative-reporting, grp.lab-report and grp.empirical-project-report should take dat.data-commentary as a prerequisite. tst.test-vs-university is the natural place to cross-reference the IELTS Task 1 versus data commentary contrast.

Gap: no topic covers commentary on qualitative or mixed-methods displays (coding frames, thematic maps, joint displays). The data commentary literature is quantitatively biased; consider a scope note on dat.data-commentary or a link from res.qualitative-reporting.
Gap: the tool skill of producing charts in spreadsheet or statistics software is assumed by dat.creating-visuals but not modelled anywhere.

edt.editing-tools and dig.automated-feedback-tools overlap heavily (and both touch gai.language-support). Suggest EDT keeps spelling and grammar checking as one step in editing, while DIG covers AWE systems and AI feedback features, including policy; or merge the two topics.

dig.machine-translation versus rdp.plurilingual-reading, wpr.l1-in-composing and src.multilingual-sources: I left these unlinked to avoid cross-group cycles. Recommend that all three take dig.machine-translation as a soft prerequisite (MT literacy, including error awareness and policy, before applying MT to reading, composing and translating sources).
dig.digital-etiquette overlaps prg.messaging-channels; suggest prg.messaging-channels <- dig.digital-etiquette (soft) or a merge.
dig.word-processing overlaps wpr.formatting. I linked only dig.word-processing <- grp.report-conventions (soft); wpr.formatting could take dig.word-processing as a soft prerequisite.
dig.vle has little language content and is institution-specific; consider moving it to ACU or LRN, or reframing it as reading assessment information on the VLE.

Gap: no PGR topic covers research data management (data management plans, FAIR principles, secure storage of participant data); dig.file-management is stretched to cover it. Suggest a new topic or a link from int.research-integrity.
cit.accuracy-consistency could take dig.reference-managers as a soft prerequisite, and gai.verifying-output overlaps the reference-verification activity under dig.reference-managers.
dig.file-management is left as a deliberate entry point with no prerequisites.
prs.posters (presenting and discussing a poster) and mmd.poster-design (designing it) are complementary; recommend prs.posters <- mmd.poster-design.
prs.recorded-online overlaps mmd.digital-assessments. I linked mmd.digital-assessments <- prs.recorded-online (soft); PRS should not link back.
prs.slide-design could take mmd.multimodal-literacy and mmd.accessibility as soft prerequisites.
mmd.accessibility is scoped in the skeleton as documents; I extended it to slides and audio-visual media (captions, transcripts). Suggest renaming it to Accessible academic documents and media.
Visual or graphical abstracts sit between mmd.infographics and res.abstracts; I have covered them under mmd.infographics.

sen.numbers-units-style overlaps num.number-expressions and num.units-measurement. Suggest SEN keeps style-guide mechanics (numerals versus words, ranges, en dashes) and NUM keeps grammar, meaning and SI conventions. Recommended direction: sen.numbers-units-style <- num.number-expressions (soft). I did not link the two, to avoid a cross-group cycle.
prn.numbers-aloud should take num.number-expressions (and, for STEM learners, num.mathematical-expression) as a prerequisite rather than the reverse.

num.approximation versus sta.hedging: approximators are one category of hedge. I deliberately did not make num.approximation depend on sta.hedging, so that sta.hedging can take num.approximation as a soft prerequisite if the STA authors wish.

crt.correlation-causation is a soft prerequisite of both num.interpreting-statistics and dat.data-commentary. CRT should not make it depend on either; num.statistical-vocabulary would be a safe soft prerequisite for it.
dse.mathematical-writing should depend on num.mathematical-expression, and res.quantitative-reporting on num.interpreting-statistics.
